data.title: The Best Books of 2026 on Healthy Aging — WSJ
data.description:
By Diane Cole

As life expectancies lengthen, there is no time like the present to develop a blueprint for the future, including ways to help sustain your health — both physical and fiscal — and maintain a sense of purpose, engagement and wonder.

Tips and advice on all those matters abound in this year's best books on healthy aging.

"Your Retirement Sketchbook: 125 Retirement Planning Lessons from Financial Experts"

By Jamie P. Hopkins and Bonnie Treichel

"There are no commandments or universal laws for retirement," write Jamie P. Hopkins and Bonnie Treichel in their compilation of retirement wisdom. "Instead of aiming for perfection, consider it a flexible, evolving outline — something you can redraw" and rework as years pass and needs and circumstances change.

That theme runs throughout the guide written by Hopkins, chief executive of Bryn Mawr Trust Advisors, and Treichel, founder of Endeavor Retirement. Accessible, practical and comprehensive, their book eschews charts and graphs to instead include cartoonlike illustrations that summarize and sketch out major points to encourage readers to envision their futures.

In addition to covering the pros and cons of various kinds of savings accounts and investment portfolios, the book reminds readers to be aware of and prepare for the potential impact of life events such as divorce and health challenges, as well as inflation. Perhaps most important: Perform periodic retirement checkups to gauge how you might want, or need, to adapt to any changes life brings.

"On Retirement: How Aging Is Transforming American Lives"

By Daniel Horowitz

In this overview of the past, present and future of retirement, cultural historian and Smith College emeritus professor Daniel Horowitz explores the impact of cultural, medical, demographic and political currents on how we may expect to spend our post-50 decades.

Horowitz reviews the ways in which medical advances have translated into longer and healthier lifespans — and raises concerns about what that may mean for the financial well-being of those already struggling. He reflects on the continuing relevance of psychoanalyst Erik Erikson's framing of old age as a still-vital life stage and exposes the false assumptions and stereotypes that can make senior citizens feel invisible.

His chapter surveying how aging and retirement have been depicted on screen over the decades will add many titles to your watch, or rewatch, list. Among the films: "Dodsworth" (1936), focused on the perils of retiring too early; "Harry and Tonto" (1974), the charming chronicle of 72-year-old Harry's cross-country road trip with his cat, Tonto; and "The Bucket List" (2007), a tale of two older men whose differing backgrounds don't stop them from waxing philosophical and making the most of the limited time they have left.

"When Memory Fades: What to Expect at Every Stage, From Early Signs to Full Support for Alzheimer's and Dementia"

By Nathaniel Chin, M.D.

"What would you do if this were your father?" That is the question the adult children of older parents showing memory-loss symptoms routinely ask Alzheimer's researcher Nathaniel Chin. This book is his answer, blending his medical expertise with his story of caring for his father as he lived, and ultimately died, of Alzheimer's.

Chin, a geriatrician and memory-clinic doctor, begins by explaining that dementia isn't itself a disease, but rather an umbrella term used to describe someone's persistent cognitive and functional decline. Still, it isn't a normal or inevitable part of aging. Nor is it the same as Alzheimer's, which is a disease. Moreover, Alzheimer's and other brain diseases can coexist, a condition referred to as mixed dementia.

Chin emphasizes the importance of early and continual monitoring of any troubling symptoms. Look out, for instance, for problems with attention, memory, language, reasoning, or getting or feeling lost in familiar places. Early detection can provide both patients and caregivers time to take in, adjust, and prepare for a new reality. It's also important for being able to benefit from new medications that can help slow the disease's progress but only at an early stage.

"Faster Than You at 60: The Inspiring Backstories of the Fastest Masters Athletes in the World"

By Graham Broyd

It's never too late to enter a track meet, author Graham Broyd discovered when he became a competitive runner at age 56. Now in his late 60s, the former banking executive is far from alone in finding purpose and enjoyment participating as an amateur in senior games around the world.

The backgrounds of each of the 22 men and women he profiles differ. What unites them is that despite their inability to pursue their athletic dreams and goals when young, they found their way back to competitive athletics in their 50s and beyond. The benefits to be gained, Broyd has found, include continued health and fitness, a sense of purpose and the camaraderie of belonging to a community.

Perhaps the most inspiring story is that of Brian Hankerson, who from childhood wanted to be a high-jumper but was too short — he was only 5 feet, 2 inches at high-school graduation. Ten inches taller by the end of college, he took 30 more years to rediscover his love of track while helping train his children and their teammates. Hooked, he began intensive training and entered seniors' competitions, culminating in an age 65-69 division champion win in 2025 over Olympian and track great Willie Banks.

"More Rules for Aging: Making the Most of Your Ridiculous, Wondrous Life"

By Roger Rosenblatt

Author and essayist Roger Rosenblatt's follow-up to "Rules for Aging," published 25 years ago, is part laugh-out-loud funny, part practical advice, and sweet and spicy throughout. His main point, he writes, is that "old age is a rich and surprising time of life, whenever one is not seeing doctors."

He describes his sense of wonder upon witnessing a 2024 eclipse of the sun: "Something occurs beyond rational comprehension...and we gape open-mouthed." He praises the power of small talk: "Most people, including myself, don't have half a dozen big issues they know anything about. Whereas in contrast, everyone can say hi and how are you....We say absolutely nothing and are delighted to say it. It's what makes the world go round, peacefully, nice and slow."

He can be blunt, reminding readers to get over their self-absorption: "No one can be interesting all the time. Not even you." As for regrets, he says, "They're part of life. Learn to live with them."

Whether read in bits and pieces, or all at once, Rosenblatt's wry sagacity will spark a smile.

Write to reports@wsj.com

data.title: Spacecraft begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
data.description:
By Will Dunham

After an eight-year journey, the European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo has begun orbiting the solar system's smallest and innermost planet Mercury, though the European Space Agency said on Sunday a glitch has occurred involving its thrusters.

Mercury, only slightly larger than Earth's moon, is the least explored of the four planets in the inner solar system, with BepiColombo only the third spacecraft to visit the planet and just the second to orbit it.

It is a joint mission of the European Space Agency, or ESA, and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, or JAXA.

ESA confirmed on Saturday that BepiColombo had begun its orbit. In a social media post on Sunday, ESA said the spacecraft had a successful entry into orbit, but during the maneuver, "the thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue."

"The spacecraft is safe and teams at ESOC (the European Space Operations Centre) are working to understand what happened," ESA said, adding that "updates will be provided on Monday."

The robotic spacecraft, launched in 2018, is a composite of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, which have different scientific objectives and are due to separate on December 9 and 10. Routine science operations are slated to commence in April.

The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface.

Mercury's surface looks similar to that of the moon, with numerous impact craters. There are expanses of smooth terrain as well as cliffs, some up to a mile (1.6 km) tall.

Mercury is about 60% closer to the sun than Earth. That means that from its surface, the sun appears more than three times as large and seven times as luminous as it does when seen from Earth. Mercury's diameter of 3,032 miles (4,880 km) is less than 40% of Earth's diameter of 7,926 miles (12,753 km).

Clariant and Ashland declined to comment on the report. CD&R could not immediately be reached for comment.

data.title: 'Hunger Games' helps box office rebound amid GTA 6 fever
data.description:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping brought audiences back to Panem in force, opening with an estimated $120M domestically and helping lift the overall box office sharply from the prior weekend.

Lionsgate’s latest entry in the franchise debuted at No. 1 from 4,018 locations, averaging about $29,866 per theater. The film added $105M internationally for a $225M worldwide opening and generated $26.4M globally from IMAX , the biggest IMAX debut in franchise history.

The broader domestic marketplace collected an estimated $168.08M across 39 reported titles, up 89.5% from the prior weekend but down 8.2% from the comparable 2025 frame, when Wicked: For Good opened to $147M. The top 10 accounted for about $158.31M. Domestic box-office revenue for 2026 now stands at $8.97B, up 20.4% from the comparable period last year and roughly $1.03B short of $10B.

For investors tracking theatrical demand through ticket receipts, the weekend offered a notable rebound ahead of Thanksgiving, even with the launch of Take-Two Interactive’s Grand Theft Auto VI competing for consumers’ entertainment time.

Rentrak’s Paul Dergarabedian said speculation that GTA VI would hurt The Hunger Games appeared misplaced, arguing that “both can do just fine.”

Rocky punches into second

Amazon MGM Studios’ I Play Rocky expanded from limited release into 2,477 theaters and collected an estimated $9.33M, good for second place. Its domestic total reached $10.42M. The film also earned an A+ CinemaScore, a rare mark of strong audience approval.

Paramount’s Ebenezer, last weekend’s No. 1 film, slipped to third with $7.7M, down about 60% in its second weekend. Its domestic total reached $32.5M, with another $45.9M internationally.

Warner Bros.’ The Cat in the Hat placed fourth with $6.9M, followed by Godzilla Minus Zero at $2.7M.

The remainder of the top 10 was tightly packed. You Can See Everything and Wild Horse Nine each collected about $2.5M, followed by Sony’s Ghost Soldier at $2.4M, Wildwood at $2.3M and Ramayana at $2.1M.

Thanksgiving next

Studios now turn to the five-day Thanksgiving frame, when several new releases will challenge Sunrise on the Reaping. Disney’s Hexed and Universal’s Focker in Law open wide Wednesday, while Neon expands Paper Tiger and Netflix begins an exclusive IMAX run for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Angel Studios’ Hershey opens Thanksgiving Day.

Last year’s five-day Thanksgiving period generated $290.31M domestically. The record remains $424.9M from 2024, when Moana 2 contributed $225.44M.

data.title: GTA VI Has Better Taste Than Your Discover Weekly
data.description:
The record that sells me on Stockyard FM is LCD Soundsystem’s “North American Scum.” If you’re going to put a song about the embarrassment of being American in a game that sells the rest of the world a fantasy of being American, that’ll do nicely. You could put it under a shot of a beautiful condo rising behind a petrol station and get most of the way through an essay about Florida before the first chorus. On the same station are Caribou’s “Never Come Back” and Fischerspooner’s “Emerge.” Someone was willing to let those three tastes sit in the same car. Rockstar’s credits have The Dare playing Harrison and PinkPantheress playing Victoria on the mic.

[embed]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gJ2np7R-Uwg[/embed]

LCD Soundsystem’s official video for “North American Scum,” one of the tracks on Stockyard FM.

I’d be perfectly happy if Discover Weekly put any of those records in my Monday queue. That’s part of my problem with it. I’m a dangerously easy man to please if you know which ten songs I’ve played to death. Eventually a playlist made from my habits starts to resemble the cupboard I open every night expecting it to contain something different.

What the DJ heard in it

Played on their own, those Stockyard records get filed under different moods. “Emerge” has the hard, slightly ridiculous glamour of electroclash. Caribou is warmer, a dance record that keeps drawing you back to the same phrase. LCD Soundsystem turns a national identity crisis into something you can shout along to. The station makes room for the joke, the mood and the beat. The connection makes sense once someone makes it for you, which is a big part of the pleasure of hearing somebody else pick records.

Put three good records in a folder and you have three good records. Put the wrong one on at the right moment and people will ask you what it was. Anyone who’s played records to a room knows the next ten minutes can change how the previous ten sounded. A person walking onto the dance floor has to decide whether they trust you. Give them everything they already wanted and you’ll probably have a pleasant night. One person might even remember it.

The original Vice City understood this well enough that Rockstar and Sony released seven soundtrack albums in 2002, each built around a station. You could take that fictional station home without the driving or the cops. Years later, Rockstar’s music director Ivan Pavlovich, who founded the Chicago deep-house label Guidance Recordings, explained how the studio worked on GTA V. “We license way more music than we use,” he told The Guardian. Anyone who’s come home from a record shop with a stack of good records and then left half of them in the bag before a set knows that feeling. Choosing what to leave out is a large part of the job.

As requested by your previous self

Spotify says Discover Weekly had generated more than 100 billion track streams by its tenth anniversary in 2025. In the anniversary post, it calls the selections “handpicked just for them.” The service has put plenty of people onto artists they would never have heard otherwise. Ordinarily I’m delighted when a computer turns up a useful record and requires nothing in return beyond knowing a disturbing amount about my Tuesday nights.

But Spotify’s two important words there are for them. Its promise is that my next discovery will fit me. Stockyard FM serves a different purpose. A player who found Fischerspooner last week and someone who bought the single when it came out can turn on the same station. The records sound different to each person. They have something to talk about anyway.

What Rockstar has at its disposal is context Spotify can only guess at. The scenery and the soundtrack inhabit the same world. “North American Scum” has a different job playing in a car in Vice City than it has as the fourth song on a playlist called Indie Dance Party. One of the cheapest ways to change a scene in a film is to change the record under it. Radio lets a player blunder into the same effect on the way to a petrol station.

Of course, Rockstar has a commercial use for all of this. There’s a separate 34-track album of original music to stream or buy. BNC has already covered what the company sold you in the game box. It’s perfectly possible to enjoy the radio while noticing that the record shop and the car dealership have the same owner.

Still, I’m glad somebody in Vice City is prepared to put on a record I might turn off. For a song to change your mind, there has to be a moment when you’re pretty sure it won’t. Give it until the next set of lights.

data.title: A Wealthy Woman and Her Chicago Neighbors Are at War Over Rats — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Cadenhead and Joe Barrett

CHICAGO — Katherine Getz started seeing them in April on her early morning walks through the sprawling green space of Lincoln Park: People outfitted with identical latex gloves and Army-green satchels, tossing handfuls of nuts on the ground for squirrels.

And not just a few peanuts.

"That doesn't look indigenous," she recalled thinking. "That's not some cute little acorn; they're the size of a small chicken egg."

She thought it was weird but didn't give it much more thought — until the rats showed up.

Rat burrows at the base of trees have spread in some areas of the park, neighbors say. At dawn and dusk, the rodents swarm the area. On a recent Saturday at the farmers market, Getz saw a rat "jump across a path over the feet of marketgoers," she said. "Right past the grilled cheese stand."

People have long scattered breadcrumbs or dropped popcorn for wildlife in city parks.

But residents and public officials in Lincoln Park, the well-heeled North Side neighborhood, suspect something different is afoot in the 1,200-acre park of the same name.

They believe the wife of a reclusive business magnate has enlisted the nut-tossing crew to satisfy her deep love of squirrels, inadvertently fueling a rat infestation that is making life miserable for everyone else.

Local alderman Timmy Knudsen started receiving complaints in 2023 about a house just two blocks from the park. Neighbors say the homeowners, instead of putting up a bird feeder, had turned the house into one over the previous two years.

They had nuts piled on the wall surrounding the house and affixed to the trunks of trees. Pounds of seed were scattered on the roof.

Squirrels, pigeons and rats loved it. Neighbors not so much.

"It's stranger than fiction," he said.

It got stranger. Knudsen soon discovered the house is owned by Barre and Barbara Seid.

Barre Seid, the 94-year-old former owner of Tripp Lite, is known for his prolific donations to conservative causes, including a $1.6 billion gift to a conservative political advocacy group, but he keeps a low public profile. Many neighbors say they've never met him. But a few have encountered his wife Barbara, a 69-year-old opera singer known for feeding the neighborhood dogs.

"She's always been super friendly and maybe a little eccentric," said neighbor Alex Huegle. The ample supply of treats at the house have made it a must-stop for his dog, Benny. "It becomes every dog's favorite thing," he said.

Laura Watson's dog got so excited about treats at the Seids' house that he once ran inside the front door. When she ran in after him, she was struck by the gigantic bags of nuts in the foyer.

"I can't even describe how many pounds of nuts it was," Watson said.

Knudsen sent letters asking the Seids to stop feeding the animals, but never received a response. The Department of Streets and Sanitation followed up with a series of $300 fines, which the couple paid.

But the staff never stopped leaving out nuts and seeds, Knudsen said. Soon, locals reported seeing staff members heading toward the park to expand the feeding. Some have tried to confront them. It hasn't always gone well.

When David Pike and his wife recently ran across the group and asked them what they were doing, they got a terse answer: "They said, 'None of your f — ing business,'" said Pike.

Several neighbors said they've seen Barbara Seid with a satchel scattering nuts in the park.

Knudsen said he's discussing potential legal action with city lawyers since tickets aren't working. "Someone who has an unlimited amount of money isn't even going to blink at them," he said.

The Chicago Park District, meanwhile, has placed "Do Not Feed Wildlife" signs throughout the park and requested stepped up rat-abatement efforts by Streets and Sanitation.

A man who answered the door at the family's home in early November said Barbara Seid was out of the country, but that she had stopped feeding the squirrels in the park about a month earlier, when the controversy first started to swirl.

"We weren't the only ones doing it," said the man, who declined to be identified. "If someone is out there, it's not us."

In a written response to questions from the Journal, Barbara Seid didn't address the specific allegations against her. "I do not believe unrelated side conversations or exaggerated allegations should become the defining narrative about me," she said.

"I genuinely love these animals: Dogs, cats, squirrels, and birds, which are all part of the environment I appreciate," Seid said. "I have never hidden that affection, nor do I see anything unusual about it."

Seth Magle, senior director of the Urban Wildlife Institute at Lincoln Park Zoo, which sits at ground zero of the squirrel-feeding activities, said squirrels are thriving in the city without extra help from humans.

"They certainly don't need any food subsidies from us," he said on a recent day as he walked past shells from Brazil nuts, peanuts, walnuts, macadamia nuts and pecans. "Feeding wildlife never ends well."

Some residents aren't bothered by the operation.

"Since I saw 'Ratatouille,' I'm OK with rats," said Bill Griffin, a lobbyist, who's noticed on walks with his dog, Ozzy, the rise in the rat population since the feeding started. "I don't want to knock anybody on their hobbies."

To Arielle Corbett, it's just part of city living. "If they get some nuts from somebody, great," said the boat caretaker, out with a friend's dogs on a recent day. "It's probably healthier than some of the other things they're eating out here. Old rib tips, bags of chips and half-eaten sandwiches."

But others just can't understand why someone would shell out to feed wild animals.

Caroline Novak encountered the group tossing nuts in the park last fall, and approached one of them.

"I said in a very friendly way, 'Why are you throwing these nuts down?'" Novak said. "And she replied by saying, 'We're not feeding the rats,' which was the most bizarre response."

The group moved on to a different part of the park. "They started throwing the nuts out faster as they walked away," Novak added.

data.title: Fujitsu launches pilot study with FamilyMart to analyze decarbonized product purchasing behavior and create demand using causal AI
data.description:
KAWASAKI, Japan, Nov 22, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Fujitsu Limited today announced that it has launched a pilot study in collaboration with FamilyMart Co., Ltd. (FamilyMart) to analyze consumer purchasing behavior and establish a demand creation model for decarbonized products [1]. The study combines "Fujitsu Causal AI"-a core technology of Fujitsu's AI platform, "Fujitsu Kozuchi"-with LLM causal technology [2]. This initiative is part of the "Model Project for Creating Demand for Decarbonized Products" [3], a program publicly solicited by Japan's Ministry of the Environment.

While the development and supply of decarbonized products are progressing, it remains unclear to what extent consumers recognize their environmental value or how this recognition influences their purchasing decisions. Furthermore, challenges persist in understanding how various factors-such as functionality, price, marketing content, and information touchpoints-interact to influence purchasing decisions.

In this pilot study, Fujitsu and FamilyMart will focus on environmentally friendly innerwear sold by FamilyMart. Using "Fujitsu Causal AI" combined with LLM causal technology, the partners will analyze sales data and survey results collected through FamilyMart's "Famipay" app. This analysis will clarify how information and consumer touchpoints help customers understand a product's environmental value and lead to a purchase. Based on these results, the companies will implement in-store initiatives to verify their effectiveness and aim to establish a robust demand creation model. The insights and analytical methods gained are expected to be applied to other categories beyond apparel, including food, daily necessities, and household goods.

The companies will continue to discuss methods for effectively communicating environmental value and optimizing retail environments. Furthermore, Fujitsu and FamilyMart will explore the application of "Fujitsu Causal AI" to other product categories, aiming to enhance promotional activities and merchandising for a broader range of products. By doing so, the partners aim to contribute to the creation of demand for decarbonized products and enhance customer value in the retail sector through advanced, data-driven marketing.

Pilot Study Overview

- Purpose:

The Ministry of the Environment's model project aims to promote investment and innovation in decarbonization and to encourage consumer selection of these products, thereby fostering market formation. This pilot project will analyze the factors leading to the selection of decarbonized products to develop effective measures.

- Period:

November, 2026 - February, 2027

- Location:

"Famima!!" stores

- Subject Products:

Environmentally friendly wear items made with recycled polyester fibers, which reduce CO2 emissions compared to conventional synthetic fibers (a 15% reduction for inner T-shirts and an 8% reduction for REHEAT):

- "Convenience Wear Inner T-Shirt Crew Neck (White)"

- "Convenience Wear Heat-Generating & Insulating Inner REHEAT (Round Neck)" and other tops made with recycled polyester

[1] Decarbonized Products:

Products and services that contribute to decarbonization.

[2] LLM Causal Technology:

A technology that discovers intervention points by having an LLM complement intermediate factors not present in the quantitative data, based on causal relationships estimated from the data.

[3] "Model Project for Creating Demand for Decarbonized Products":

A pilot project to appropriately display the decarbonization value of products/services and develop an environment where consumers and procurement entities can understand and evaluate such value, thereby assessing the tolerance for price premiums and impacts on purchasing behavior.

data.title: New Three-Year Real-World LEQEMBI(R) Data Presented at CTAD 2026
data.description:
TOKYO and CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Nov 22, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Eisai Co., Ltd. and Biogen Inc. (Nasdaq: BIIB) today announced new three-year real-world findings of 560 patients across 13 U.S. clinical sites from the largest analysis of the ongoing Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (LEADER) study* reported to date. New LEADER findings from a pre-specified analysis show a 76% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe Alzheimer's disease dementia with LEQEMBI(R) compared to a matched natural history cohort. The data were presented alongside an additional international real-world meta-analysis of approximately 5,000 patients at the 19th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) Conference in Boston.

"As Alzheimer's disease progresses, patients and families can experience increasing challenges that affect cognition and function," said Brent Berry, M.D., Ph.D., Minneapolis Clinic of Neurology. "The LEADER study is helping us understand how the benefits of continued LEQEMBI treatment seen in the Clarity AD clinical trial carry over into routine clinical practice. These real-world findings from sites across the U.S. suggest that continued treatment with LEQEMBI may help keep patients in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease for longer. They also add to our understanding of treatment persistence, subcutaneous maintenance therapy and safety across diverse clinical settings, which can help inform treatment decisions with patients and families."

Key Findings from the LEADER Study

LEADER Patients Showed Slower Progression Compared to ADNI Control**

- In a pre-specified comparison of LEADER (N=504) and an ADNI-weighted external control cohort (N=573) through 36 months, LEQEMBI patients in the study had a 76% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe AD dementia (HR 0.24; 95% CI, 0.15-0.39).

More Than 8 in 10 Patients Remained Stable or Improved***

- Among the 546 people with early AD whose change in disease stage could be assessed after an average of approximately 18 months of treatment, 81.1% of patients were reported as stable (75.8%) or improved (5.3%) compared with baseline.

- Results were generally consistent across groups defined by sex, race, ethnicity, APOE genotype and concomitant antithrombotic-use groups.

- Among all 560 patients, 87.5% remained on LEQEMBI treatment at the time of chart extraction, with an average treatment duration of approximately 19 months.

Most Patients Estimated to Remain in Early AD Through Three Years

- Among all 560 patients receiving LEQEMBI in the overall study, 95.0% were estimated to remain in the early stages of AD through three years (36 months) of treatment, based on statistical modeling of observed real-world patient data.

New Real-World Evidence Shows Complete Amyloid Clearance

- At sites performing both baseline and follow up amyloid PET data, 77% of patients (N=33 of 43 across 6 sites) became amyloid-negative at a median follow up of 18.1 months (IQR 16.4-18.7 months).

Expanding Experience with LEQEMBI Maintenance Therapy

- Of the patients who reached 18 months of treatment, 91.7% remained on LEQEMBI treatment. A total of 218 patients transitioned to once-every-four-weeks intravenous (IV) maintenance therapy and, following its subsequent approval, 64 patients transitioned to once-weekly subcutaneous (SC) maintenance therapy.

- 71.1% of patients on monthly IV maintenance treatment and 76.6% on weekly SC maintenance treatment remained stable after an average of 26 months and 25.1 months following treatment initiation, respectively.

- All 64 patients receiving SC maintenance therapy remained on therapy at the time of chart extraction.

- No ARIA**** events were reported during the subcutaneous maintenance period and there were no other safety events of significance. There was a 0.5% incidence of isolated ARIA-H reported during the IV maintenance period.

Clinical Outcomes Consistent Between Women and Men

- 79.3% of women (N=300) and 83.3% of men (N=246) in the study were reported as stable or improved***.

- Treatment duration and persistence were similar across sexes, with 86.0% of females and 88.9% of males remaining on therapy at time of chart extraction.

- ARIA incidence and severity were generally consistent between female and male patients: any ARIA (14.7% females vs. 17.0% males), ARIA-E (7.5% females vs. 5.5% males), ARIA-H (9.8% females vs. 12.6% males), isolated ARIA-H (7.2% females vs. 11.5% males).

LEADER Safety Findings Consistent with ALZ-NET Real-World Experience

Overall safety findings in LEADER were consistent with the independent ALZ-NET registry and U.S. prescribing information for LEQEMBI.

- ALZ-NET is a North American voluntary health care provider-enrolled patient network that collects longitudinal clinical, imaging, and safety data in patients treated with FDA-approved AD therapies. Over 1,700 patients taking LEQEMBI were included in ALZ-NET at the time of data extraction.

- ARIA-E was observed in 6.6% of patients in LEADER, compared with 6.3% in ALZ-NET, while ARIA-H was observed in 11.1% of patients in LEADER, compared with 10.1% of patients in ALZ-NET.

- Observed ARIA rates were generally consistent regardless of APOE ε4 status, concomitant antithrombotic use, race and ethnicity.

Additional International Real-World Meta-Analysis Evaluates Approximately 5,000 Patients*****

A separate post hoc-exploratory analysis presented at CTAD evaluated 16 published real-world LEQEMBI cohorts across six countries, representing approximately 5,000 patients treated in routine clinical practice.

Key findings include:

- Rates of ARIA were lower than those reported in Clarity AD. Across the 16 real-world studies, the pooled average total ARIA rate was 12.4% compared to 21.5% in Clarity AD, ARIA-E rate was 4.0% compared to 12.6% in Clarity AD, and the ARIA-H rate was 9.4% compared to 17.3% in Clarity AD.

- Symptomatic ARIA was 0.8% compared to 2.8% in Clarity AD.

- Treatment discontinuation due to adverse events was 3.2%.

* The three-year LEADER Study is a multicenter, retrospective real-world study designed to examine LEQEMBI utilization, treatment persistence, transition to maintenance therapy, safety, cognitive and functional assessments, and healthcare professional (HCP) implementation learnings in diverse U.S. clinical settings for patients with early AD. The study integrated deidentified chart and electronic medical record (EMR) data from 13 U.S. sites, HCP surveys and HCP interviews. This updated analysis included 560 patients with early AD who, as of September 2026, received at least seven LEQEMBI initiation infusions. The maintenance therapy analysis included patients who received biweekly IV initiation treatment for 18 months, followed by at least three months of IV or SC maintenance therapy.

** ADNI is a clinical research project launched in 2005 to develop methods to predict the onset and progression of AD and to confirm the effectiveness of treatments. The project involves a multi-year longitudinal observation targeting healthy elderly individuals as well as patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and early stages of AD.

*** Change in clinical disease stage was defined as:

- Stable: Patient remaining in the same clinical disease stage (MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia) from baseline throughout the course of LEQEMBI treatment.

- Improvement: Patient transitioning from mild AD dementia at baseline to MCI due to AD over the course of LEQEMBI treatment.

- Progression: Patient advancing from MCI at baseline to mild/moderate AD dementia or from mild AD dementia at baseline to moderate AD dementia throughout the course of LEQEMBI treatment.

**** ARIA refers to amyloid-related imaging abnormalities that can be observed with anti-amyloid beta antibody treatment and includes ARIA-E, which involves edema/effusion, and ARIA-H, which involves hemosiderin deposition, including cerebral microhemorrhage, cerebral macrohemorrhage and superficial siderosis, as observed on brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

***** The meta-analysis on ARIA rates and safety profiles in clinical practice included centers located in the U.S., China, South Korea, Japan, Italy and Israel. Patients were treated between 2023 and 2026 and received at least six months of LEQEMBI treatment.

data.title: Goldman watching for 3 conditions that could support a stock correction bottom
data.description:
Goldman Sachs is watching for three potential catalysts that could signal a bottom in the current equity correction and set the stage for a market recovery.

The S&P 500 has fallen 12% from its Oct. 6 record high, exceeding the median 10% calendar-year peak-to-trough decline seen since 1980. The Nasdaq 100 has dropped 20%. Historically, following 22 S&P 500 corrections of at least 10% since 1980, the index gained an average 4% over the next three months, rising in 73% of those episodes.

Goldman said the first condition it is watching for is news that increases investor confidence in the outlook for earnings tied to AI investment and monetization.

The second would be an improvement in the macro backdrop, including a dovish signal from the Federal Reserve.

The third would be a significant further decline in investor positioning, a feature that has often accompanied previous market bottoms.

That last condition has not yet been met broadly. Hedge funds have sold heavily in recent weeks, with net leverage dropping to its lowest level since April 2025, but Goldman’s broader measure of equity positioning remains above average.

The firm’s U.S. Equity Sentiment Indicator, which combines nine measures of positioning across institutional, retail and foreign investors, stood at 0.7 as of Nov. 20. Meanwhile, U.S. equity mutual funds and ETFs have attracted nearly $170B of inflows since the start of Q4, while asset-manager equity futures positioning ranks in the 82nd percentile of the past decade.

The selloff has also broadened beyond AI. Goldman’s AI basket has fallen 32% since Oct. 6, while the S&P 500 excluding AI is now 6% below its high, and cyclical stocks have begun underperforming defensives as investors mark down expectations for economic growth.

Despite the correction, Goldman still forecasts the S&P 500 reaching 8,700 over the next 12 months.

data.title: AI Rout Turns Gold Into Source Of Cash: What Comes Next?
data.description:
Gold fell to a 14-month low on Friday as a rout in technology shares prompted investors to sell bullion to cover losses elsewhere. The metal slid alongside falling Treasury yields and the US dollar.

Spot gold fell to $3,502 an ounce- the lowest level since September 2025. In total, bullion lost 8.9% for the week, while the Invesco QQQ ETF sank 9.31% and State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:SPY) fell by 7.98%, entering correction territory

Rate Hike Bets Set the Stage

Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting showed that nearly all policymakers anticipated further rate increases. According to the CME FedWatch, traders currently price in an 88.6% chance of a quarter-point increase in December.

“The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses,” David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures, told Reuters.

Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, wrote that bullion “has become a source of cash for investors facing mounting losses elsewhere,” Mining.com reported.

In a market commentary, former Bridgewater economist Bob Elliott said pro-growth pricing “remains quite elevated” and warned the selloff could become “more self-reinforcing to the downside.”

Once downturns start, he wrote, they typically require “both much cheaper pricing and some sort of policy support to get to the bottom, neither of which we are at yet.”

Interestingly, there was little sign of a broad exit from gold funds. Holdings in gold ETFs tracked by Bloomberg were little changed over the preceding month despite a roughly 10% drop in bullion, Hansen said.

Mining shares were less resilient, since their leverage to gold price works both ways. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (NYSE:GDX) closed the week 14.80% below the previous Friday’s close. The largest names in the sector, Newmont , Barrick Mining and Agnico Eagle Mines lost 15.03%, 15.19% and 13.64%, respectively.

Technical Outlook

Gold’s daily chart shows the magnitude of the post-summer carnage. After peaking in August and briefly moving above the 200-day moving average, bullion reversed course and fell by over 25%.

Gold, daily chart, Source: TradingView

Zooming out, the next key support area is the Q2-Q3 2025 price range. For much of that time, price remained in a tight accumulation between $3,200 and $3,450.

Thus, price could easily fall further, test that range, and wait for the next catalyst to move it either way.

data.title: Chainflip’s losses climb to $12 million after protocol discloses 122.9 BTC theft, offers hacker bounty
data.description:
Cross-chain decentralized exchange Chainflip (FLIP) said an attacker took 122.86 BTC from its Bitcoin vault on Saturday, on top of the $4.86 million in ETH and stablecoins drained from its Ethereum vault that The Block reported Saturday, putting total losses at about $12 million.

Chainflip Labs, in a message to the hacker, said 122.86137042 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT were taken from its vaults. The bitcoin was worth about $7.1 million at the time of the theft.

Chainflip offers 10% bounty

In its message, which was also sent onchain, Chainflip Labs offered to let the hacker keep 10% of the proceeds and stop its law enforcement efforts if they return the remaining 90% by Monday at 1:38 p.m. ET. Chainflip also says it has identified and fixed the vulnerability that the attacker exploited, and that it has learned some details about the attacker, including identifying the server that the hacker used to register their validator account.

"You have made some mistakes in how you conducted this attack and we believe law enforcement will be able to establish an identity based on the metadata you left behind and the particular services you used," the message states. "Your addresses are flagged with the major blockchain analytics firms, which will make it extremely difficult to liquidate the proceeds of your actions, and every withdrawal from the Tornado Cash pools you used is being watched. We will pursue this as hard as we can, for as long as it takes."

Chainflip did not describe the precise mechanism the attacker exploited, though it appears to have been a compromise of the protocol's aggregate signing key. Chainflip's vaults are controlled by signing keys held jointly by a set of up to 150 validators, 100 of whom must take part to approve a transaction.

Bitcoin was stolen before ETH

The hacker stole the bitcoin from Chainflip's vault about 30 minutes before the Ethereum drain that security firms flagged on Saturday. At 1:41 a.m. ET, a single transaction moved 122.86 BTC from Chainflip's Bitcoin vault to a new address, and the funds moved again about 20 minutes later, onchain data shows.

The Block previously reported that Chainflip's Bitcoin vault appeared to be unaffected. A separate transfer that moved about 10.5 BTC from a previous Chainflip vault address to a new address at 6:24 a.m. ET, which The Block also reported, is not among the assets Chainflip listed as stolen, suggesting that movement was Chainflip preventing further losses.

The 122.86 BTC remained at the attacker's second address as of Sunday afternoon. The ETH and stablecoins taken from the Ethereum vault were swapped and sent through Tornado Cash within ten minutes in a process that appeared to be fully automated, according to blockchain security firm AMLBot.

Chainflip's founder is "relatively confident" about restart

Chainflip founder Simon Harman said on X on Sunday morning that he has been in contact with law enforcement and investigators and is "now relatively confident we can get back and running despite the significant losses to LPs." Harman said Chainflip will publish a report on the incident on Monday and that ideas for compensation are still being worked on.

Chainflip's website says its services are temporarily unavailable. FLIP traded at about $0.30 on Sunday afternoon, down about 37% from its level before the attack, according to The Block's Chainflip price page.

In September, Chainflip lost about 736,000 USDT when an attacker abused a flaw in how the protocol processed Tron transaction memos. Its validators later voted to reimburse affected liquidity providers using surplus funds held in the protocol's vaults.

data.title: SA Asks: How much of a threat is Anthropic's multi-chip strategy to Nvidia?
data.description:
How much of a threat is Anthropic's multi-chip strategy, which allows its AI agents to run on multiple chip families, to Nvidia's dominance in the industry?

Seeking Alpha analysts The Techie, Victor Dergunov, Danil Sereda, and Bashar Issa weigh in.

The Techie: While I think Anthropic’s multi-chip strategy poses risks to Nvidia’s market share, I wouldn’t say it’s exactly existential to the company. As of now, six out of seven Nvidia customers are building or using custom chips, so I think the industry is already moving away, and things will get worse in 2027. We know that the frontiers will make up 15% of Nvidia’s revenue this year, and while I don’t expect that figure to decline next year, I have a hard time seeing it grow.

Victor Dergunov: I believe Anthropic's multi-chip strategy illustrates that other major chip players exist, such as Broadcom , Alphabet , Amazon , Advanced Micro Devices , and others. However, I don't believe this dynamic implies insufficient demand or that demand for Nvidia chips will likely decline in the near to intermediate term.

Danil Sereda: Anthropic is doing it right by hedging chip supplies, just like any big company does nowadays. It doesn't look like an existential threat to Nvidia’s dominance, in my understanding. Weekly token volume is surging rapidly, the whole AI market is expanding, and so are Anthropic's operations. It already scaled to an $81B annualized revenue run rate ahead of its IPO.

It's good to see them experimenting with custom silicon like Amazon's AWS Trainium and Alphabet's Google TPUs. But the demand for massive acceleration in frontier capabilities is making Nvidia the main raw throughput provider.

In fact, Nvidia's partnership with Anthropic has been expanding, with Nvidia broadening Anthropic's access to Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity across cloud providers. On its latest earnings call, Nvidia management stated it expects major frontier labs to contribute around 15% to its data center revenue this year. The Techie, another SA author, calculated next year's figure at 24%.

So, I don't see any abrupt threat to Nvidia because of Anthropic's supply hedging strategies. If there were indeed a major risk, we'd already see it in Nvidia's recent earnings revisions. There are no indications of that so far.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

Bashar Issa: Anthropic’s multi-chip strategy is naturally bad for Nvidia in the short term, but potentially good for the AI sector, including Nvidia, in the long run.

Nvidia needs to lower its prices because, at this stage, data center unit economics are distorted, in large part by high GPU costs. As mentioned in a recent article, Nvidia generates $4 in revenue for every $1 in COGS. These high margins are not sustainable.

A successful multi-chip strategy might be the catalyst needed to bring some normalization to the sector. That would put pressure on Nvidia's margins in the short term, but healthier data center economics could support more sustainable demand for its GPUs in the long run.

data.title: OpenAI calls for industry-wide AI brake tied to perplexity
data.description:
OpenAI is calling for frontier AI developers to adopt common limits on model development tied partly to perplexity, arguing that improvements in the metric can foreshadow the emergence of powerful and unpredictable new capabilities.

In a post Sunday, OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed an industry standard that would establish measurable thresholds developers agree not to cross until corresponding advances are made in understanding and monitoring AI behavior .

Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token, with lower readings representing better performance. OpenAI generally tracks its logarithm, also known as cross-entropy loss, and Pachocki argued that the measure has remained unusually useful for tracking the underlying intelligence created during pretraining even as downstream AI benchmarks rapidly become obsolete.

OpenAI said GPT-3.5 registered log-perplexity of about 0.99 on its main internal evaluation dataset, while GPT-4 reached about 0.91. As losses moved below 0.8, the company began seeing transformative capabilities in areas including cybersecurity and mathematics. A model at roughly 0.76 began producing what Pachocki described as groundbreaking mathematical results.

Looking ahead, Pachocki said OpenAI expects further transformative capabilities as models move into roughly the 0.68-0.70 range, although the company does not know what those capabilities will be.

That uncertainty underpins the proposed development limits. Pachocki said frontier labs should agree on shared evaluation and red-teaming standards and establish a first threshold they would not cross until monitoring technology reached a defined milestone, such as a successor to current chain-of-thought monitoring systems.

The proposal comes as OpenAI sees AI beginning to contribute to its own development. Pachocki said an acceleration in pretraining research could emerge as soon as 2027 if AI systems begin generating fundamental algorithmic advances, potentially speeding progress faster than alignment and monitoring techniques can keep pace.

OpenAI acknowledged that perplexity is an imperfect common standard. Results can be difficult to compare between laboratories because developers use different datasets and training mixtures, and perplexity does not capture all capability gains, including those produced by chain-of-thought reasoning.

Still, Pachocki argued that greater transparency around the measure could provide the industry with a shared scientific basis for pacing increasingly capable AI systems.

data.title: Delta flights faced brief delays at Atlanta airport over automated system issue
data.description:
Delta Air Lines experienced brief delays on flights to and from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the busiest in the US.

Here are some details:

  • The airline said in a statement that it was using "manual workarounds" to safely dispatch flights while efforts continued to restore automation for departing flight weight and balance calculations.

  • The company also said it was working with air traffic control counterparts to ease congestion at its Atlanta hub.

  • The US Federal Aviation Administration briefly issued a ground stop because of the issue, resulting in delays of about an hour before it was lifted. The FAA said the disruption was not related to any FAA air traffic systems.

  • Weight and balance calculations are required before takeoff to ensure an aircraft remains within safety limits and maintains a proper center of gravity for stable flight, according to the FAA.

  • The disruption comes after a US router outage triggered a nationwide ground stop on November 13 that disrupted more than 18,000 flights and affected about 1 million passengers.

data.title: Joint Proposal Selected for the Space Strategy Fund Project "Development and Demonstration of General-Purpose Ground Antennas and Use Cases to Expand the Utilization of Satellite Communications"
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 22, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Sharp Corporation, Saitama University, ARAV Inc., Prodrone Co., Ltd., and FURUNO ELECTRIC CO., LTD., together with Institute of Science Tokyo, jointly submitted a proposal for a technology development theme under the Space Strategy Fund for which the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) invited proposals. The proposal involves the development of general-purpose ground antennas compatible with 5G NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) as next-generation satellite communication terminals and the demonstration of their use in the mobility sector under "Development and Demonstration of General-Purpose Ground Antennas and Use Cases to Expand the Utilization of Satellite Communications". The joint proposal was selected on October 30, 2026.

About the Space Strategy Fund

Amid the global expansion of the space market, the Space Strategy Fund was established at JAXA in March 2024 to provide long-term support for technology development in the space sector. The Fund supports a wide range of initiatives undertaken by private companies, universities, research institutions, and other organizations, ranging from business demonstrations to innovative technology development. It provides support over multiple years, for up to 10 years, in three areas: "Space Transportation," "Satellites," and "Space Exploration."

Development of General-Purpose Ground Antennas Supporting Multiple Satellite Communication Services

Further utilization of satellite communications is expected to help ensure stable connectivity even in areas with limited terrestrial communication network coverage, such as mountainous areas, maritime areas, and disaster-affected areas. Based on this proposal, the parties will develop a general-purpose ground antenna compatible with 5G NTN, a communications standard that applies widely adopted terrestrial 5G technology to satellite communications and is being standardized internationally. In addition, the antenna will be designed to support multiple frequency bands, with the aim of enabling a single antenna to switch between multiple satellite communication services.

Demonstration of Applications in the Mobility Sector

The general-purpose ground antennas developed under this project will be installed on vehicles, drones, construction machinery, and vessels to conduct demonstration trials of satellite communication. The trials will assess communication quality and stability while in motion and verify the potential use of satellite communications for applications such as data transmission during autonomous driving, remote inspection, and video transmission.

data.title: Compass Group plans to shift primary listing from London to New York, FT reports
data.description:
Compass Group , the world's largest caterer, plans to shift its primary listing from London to New York, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Compass Group did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

Here are some details:

  • The Surrey, England headquartered company is expected to announce it is moving its listing to New York as soon as at its full-year results on Tuesday, according to FT

  • Compass, which counts Google, Amazon and Microsoft among its clients, also provides catering and support services to the defence sector, airline lounges and data centres

  • In July, Compass said it secured $4.3 billion of new business wins over the previous 12 months, up 16% year-on-year, with half coming from first-time outsourcing clients. It also saw a modest boost in North America volumes

  • The planned move would add to pressure on London's stock market, which has struggled to attract and retain listings as companies seek access to deeper US capital markets and higher valuations
